newsitem.title: CANADA: UGG takeover would revoke voting shares.
newsitem.headline: UGG takeover would revoke voting shares.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool said on Thursday its takeover bid for outstanding common voting shares in United Grain Growers Ltd would revoke voting shares in UGG if the co-operative's members oppose the bid.
If AWP and Manitoba Pool Elevators farmer-members vote against the takeover later this month, the bid would be withdrawn, AWP chief financial officer Geoff Southwood said.
"We intend to remain cooperatives, there would be no voting shares," Southwood told a conference call.
Alberta Wheat Pool (AWP) and Manitoba Pool Elevators (MPE) farmer-members meet later this month. The meetings are closed to the public and the dates were not disclosed.
Southwood said the C$13.75 a share takeover offer for United Grain was "reasonable" but AWP and MPE would monitor any potential rival offers.
UGG shares rose to C$14 a share on the news Thursday
AWP and MPE would create a third cooperative to run Saskatchewan grain handling.

The takeover bid was made to stave off any offers by United States-based multinationals. Rumours have persisted in the past year that Nebraska-based ConAgra Inc or Illinois-based Archer Daniels Midland may be potential suitors for UGG.
The two pools would not "as yet" consider filing a legal challenge to a poison-pill provision instituted by UGG's board on February 14 that would force a 60-day waiting period, Southwood said.
The provision is triggered when a shareholder has 15 percent of UGG's outstanding limited common voting shares.
Asked whether a takover of UGG would entail delisting the shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Southwood replied: "Correct."
The pools raised their stake in UGG to 14.98 percent February 13 and plan to spend C$172 million on Thursday's bid.
The pools also announced Thursday they had entered into an irrevocable lock-up agreement with a block of shareholders holding 6.4 percent of UGG stock.

Southwood said that block of shares were not purchased but locked up in the agreement at this time. He later added that the block of shares did not put the pools over the 15 percent poison pill threshold.
"We have a legal opinion with regard to that and we see it as no problem," Southwood said.
UGG chief executive Brian Hayward told Reuters earlier the firm's board would "assess the adequacy and terms of the offer."
UGG was founded in 1906 and incorporated under a Special Act of Parliament in 1911. Southwood said the Act would not need to be amended for the takeover to proceed.

Once AWP and MPE purchase at least 75 percent of UGG's outstanding shares, they would seek continuance under Canada's Competition Act. Commodity industry players have expressed concern over the appearance of concentration in grain handling.
Sister cooperative Saskatchewan Wheat Pool was not invited to participate in the takeover, Southwood said.
"No, they have their business and we have ours," Southwood said. "Our relations with Saskatchewan Wheat Pool are very cordial on all joint ventures."
SWP has built and acquired elevators in Alberta, Manitoba.
UGG owns more than 170 Prairie elevators and has 19 percent of elevator storage capacity in Alberta, 12 percent in Saskatchewan and 20 percent in Manitoba.
MPE and AWP storage capacity in their respective provinces would rise to about two-thirds if the bid succeeds, he said.
